title: The initial Vibe Research proposal
summary: Manny proposes the paper; the AI identifies the software/research asymmetry, prior uses of the term, authorship tensions, and possible empirical work.

title: Accountability and public access
summary: The discussion sharpens the paper around distributed expertise, institutional accountability, provenance, and public access to project-grounded AI collaborators.

title: Voice discussion: responsibility, expertise, and provenance
summary: A spoken exchange develops the senior-researcher analogy, contingent access to AI expertise, and the decision to frame the practical issue around provenance rather than deserving authorship.

title: Framing the asymmetry without moralising
summary: The collaborators decide to present different treatment of vibe coding and vibe research as a descriptive puzzle, avoiding moralising or evangelising language.

title: Prevalence as an empirical question
summary: The discussion considers whether vibe research is already widespread and develops a cautious invitation to collect self-reports rather than assume prevalence.

title: First outline and Version 1
summary: After returning to text mode, Manny requests an outline and the AI supplies the first structured draft, with the asymmetry as the organising puzzle.

title: First critique and Version 2
summary: Manny requests a title, abstract, broader examples, earlier treatment of authorship, and a more concrete public-provenance account; the AI produces Version 2.

title: Major restructuring and Version 3
summary: A long structural review removes repetition, strengthens the software analogy, separates accountability from provenance, and leads to Version 3.

title: Policy citations and Version 4
summary: The collaborators refine authorship-policy claims, the three examples, and public interrogation of provenance; Version 4 and the first bibliography are produced.

title: The Casey Newton article
summary: A newly supplied Casey Newton article is analysed for its discussion of distributed editorial expertise, AI-supported writing, disclosure, and the boundary between assistance and authorship.

title: ACL policy history and Version 5
summary: The discussion investigates whether governance reflects older AI paradigms, checks ACL policy history, narrows claims to public evidence, and produces Version 5 plus a policy bibliography.

title: Precision edits and Codex handoff
summary: Detailed edits improve the responsibility/accountability distinction and concrete examples; Version 6 is prepared as a handoff for repository work by Codex.

title: Reworking the central puzzle and Version 7
summary: The abstract, transitions, ACL analysis, and Grok provenance are tightened; the revised argument is emitted as Version 7.

title: Final handoff review and Version 9
summary: Minor conceptual and mechanical issues are resolved, citations are checked, and Version 9 becomes the clean handoff document for Codex.

title: The Castle analogy and replacement introduction
summary: After Codex repository work, the collaborators develop The Castle as a framing device for making an initially comic practice institutionally legible and produce a replacement introduction.

title: Vibe coding claims and mathematical evidence
summary: A long exchange checks stronger claims about vibe coding and surveys difficult mathematical results and Go as independent evidence of substantive AI contributions.

title: Mathematics section and Version 11 changes
summary: The collaborators retain the mathematical evidence but defer Go, carefully calibrate claims, and produce replacement passages and bibliography additions.

title: Human compression and review of Version 12
summary: Manny supplies a substantially compressed Version 12; the AI endorses the three-explanation structure and identifies conceptual overstatements and mechanical corrections.

title: Final requested revision and Version 13
summary: Manny accepts the review and requests the final revision; the AI reports incorporating the agreed conceptual fixes into Version 13.
